scientific_judgment.validity_and_methods: The manuscript makes a bounded computational contribution. Direct mature-parent gap pairing addresses a class often outside the near-match budget, while the manuscript explicitly states parent exclusion from the conventional screen, censoring and failed searches, different precursor criteria, energy-model limits, cutoff sensitivity and the limited transcript set. These constraints prevent the counts from being read as a complete liability or efficacy ranking.
scientific_judgment.results_and_negative_evidence: The numerical findings emphasized by the new framing already appear in the unchanged posted-baseline body. The strongest null does not support a disease-specific excess, and predicted pairing is distinguished from duplex formation and cleavage. The altered presentation preserves these limits.
scientific_judgment.novelty_and_merit: The useful contribution is an indication-specific design and screening resource with explicit parent-transcript liabilities, register/cutoff sensitivity, and a negative null comparison. Junction-directed oligonucleotides and pre-synthesis screening are not claimed as new methods. This is modest but coherent original computational work and a reasonable Full-length research article candidate for Computational Biology and Chemistry. Wet-lab validation would address biological questions outside the claims actually made; this review does not predict editorial acceptance.
scientific_judgment.citations: The independent DOCX delta shows no added or removed reference paragraphs or substantive body citation claims. The changed abstract and supporting presentation draw on retained results and limits, so no fresh external factual claim requires a new citation campaign. The prior focused review's identifier and source checks are reused within their stated scope; the reviewer did not revalidate every cited article or refresh all literature searches.
retained_limitations: The ten-base criterion is adopted, not a measured cleavage threshold.
No disease-specific excess is resolved by 45.8% versus the 40.6% exon-terminus null.
Most modelled junctions are unreported in patients, and the in-frame panel does not establish full clinically relevant RNA-junction coverage.
Cell-model exon labels do not establish nucleotide-level design correspondence.
Unmodified DNA:RNA model differences of 26.6 and 36.0 degrees Celsius are not validated predictions or bounds for LNA/phosphorothioate reagents.
Proposed selectivity experiments and their variance assumptions remain unperformed.
No reagent has been synthesized or tested here, and delivery, efficacy and safety remain unestablished.
